chapterNote: The only psalm in the whole book titled simply 'Tehillah' — 'a Praise' — David's last composition in the Psalter and the alphabet of adoration: an acrostic, one verse per Hebrew letter, praise organized from A to Z. After it come only the five Hallelujah psalms it ignites. Its structure is a great relay: I will extol You every day forever — and one generation commends Your works to the next, fathers handing praise to sons like a baton, because His greatness is unsearchable and no single lifetime can finish the inventory. At its center stands the LORD's own Sinai self-portrait, quoted once more: gracious and compassionate, slow to anger, great in covenant love, good to ALL, His tender mercies over all He has made. The kingdom verses (11-13) gave Daniel and the Lord's Prayer their vocabulary: an everlasting kingdom, dominion through all generations. And then the psalm's tenderest stretch: the LORD upholding all who fall, raising all who are bowed down, every eye waiting on Him, His hand opening to satisfy the desire of every living thing; near to all who call on Him in truth, keeping all who love Him. It ends where David's whole life had been heading: my mouth will speak the praise of the LORD — and let all flesh bless His holy name forever and ever.

1.text: A praise-psalm of David. I will lift You high, my God, O King, and I will bless Your name forever and ever.
1.amp: David's Psalm of praise [tehillah]. I will extol [rum — exalt, lift high] You, my God [Elohim], O king [melek]; and I will bless [barak] Your name [shem] for ever [olam] and ever [ad].
1.notes: The only psalm titled Tehillah (H8416) — 'a Praise', the noun that names the whole book (Tehillim). The king of Israel addresses Elohai ha-melek, my God THE King: David files his own crown under a higher one, and signs up for olam va-ed (H5769, H5703), the double-forever.

2.text: Every single day I will bless You, and I will praise Your name forever and ever.
2.amp: Every day [yom] will I bless [barak] You; and I will praise [halal] Your name [shem] for ever [olam] and ever [ad].
2.notes: Forever is paid in day-sized installments: be-kol-yom, every day — praise as daily bread offered back. The doubled forever returns; eternity's habit is practiced one morning at a time.

3.text: Great is the LORD and greatly to be praised, and His greatness is beyond all searching out.
3.amp: Great [gadol] is the LORD [YHWH], and greatly [meod] to be praised [halal]; and His greatness [gedullah] is unsearchable ['of his greatness there is no search', cheqer, the KJV margin].
3.notes: en cheqer (H2714): no bottom to the sounding-line — the same 'unsearchable' Job and Isaiah use of His understanding (cf. Job 5:9; Isaiah 40:28). This is why the psalm needs an alphabet and the generations need a relay: gedullah (H1420) that cannot be exhausted can only be handed on.

4.text: Generation after generation will laud Your works to the next, and they will declare Your mighty acts.
4.amp: One generation [dor] shall praise [shabach — laud, commend] Your works [maaseh] to another [dor], and shall declare [nagad] Your mighty acts [geburah].
4.notes: dor le-dor (H1755): the relay verse — praise as the family business, fathers commending (shabach, H7623) His maaseh to sons before the sons can read (cf. Deuteronomy 6:7; Psalm 78:4). Every generation is one handoff from forgetting; this verse is the baton.

5.text: On the glorious splendor of Your majesty, and on Your wondrous works, I will muse and speak.
5.amp: I will speak [siach — meditate, muse] of the glorious [kabod] honour [hadar] of Your majesty [hod], and of Your wondrous [pala] works ['things, or, words', dabar, the KJV margin].
5.notes: Three splendor-words stacked — kabod, hadar, hod (H3519, H1926, H1935) — glory layered on majesty layered on splendor, because one noun cannot carry it. siach (H7878): the musing that keeps breaking into speech.

6.text: Men will tell of the might of Your awesome acts, and I will recount Your greatness.
6.amp: And men shall speak [amar] of the might [ezuz] of Your terrible acts [yare — Your awesome, fear-inspiring deeds]: and I will declare [saphar — recount] Your greatness [gedullah].
6.notes: The chorus widens — 'men shall speak', the community's voice joining — and David keeps his own part: saphar (H5608), the recounting-verb. The 'terrible acts' are the norot, the awe-deeds: Red Sea-class interventions that make nations go quiet (cf. Psalm 66:3-5).

7.text: They will pour out the memory of Your abundant goodness like a gushing spring, and sing aloud of Your righteousness.
7.amp: They shall abundantly utter [naba — bubble up, gush forth] the memory [zeker] of Your great [rav] goodness [tuv], and shall sing [ranan — ring out] of Your righteousness [tsedaqah].
7.notes: naba (H5042), the spring-verb of Psalm 19:2: testimony under artesian pressure — the zeker (H2143) of His tuv (H2898) gushing out because it cannot be capped. Goodness remembered becomes goodness sung: memory is praise's aquifer.

8.text: The LORD is gracious and full of deep compassion, slow to anger and great in covenant love.
8.amp: The LORD [YHWH] is gracious [channun], and full of compassion [rachum]; slow [arek] to anger [aph], and of great mercy ['great in mercy', gadol chesed, the KJV margin].
8.notes: Sinai's self-revelation once more (cf. Exodus 34:6; Psalm 103:8) — the sentence Israel could not stop quoting, now set into praise's alphabet at its heart: channun, rachum (H2587, H7349), the long fuse, and chesed (H2617) in the large size.

9.text: The LORD is good to all, and His tender mercies rest over everything He has made.
9.amp: The LORD [YHWH] is good [tov] to all [kol]: and His tender mercies [rachamim] are over all His works [maaseh].
9.notes: The widest mercy-sentence in the Psalter: tov la-KOL — goodness with no address list, and rachamim (H7356) spread like a canopy over kol maaseh, everything He made. Common grace in one verse: sun and rain on just and unjust alike (cf. Matthew 5:45; Acts 14:17).

10.text: All Your works will give You thanks, O LORD, and Your covenant-faithful ones will bless You.
10.amp: All Your works [maaseh] shall praise [yadah] You, O LORD [YHWH]; and Your saints [chasid — Your covenant-loyal ones] shall bless [barak] You.
10.notes: Two choirs in one verse: creation's — every maaseh giving thanks by being what it is — and the chasidim's (H2623), the covenant-loved who bless on purpose. The works praise by existing; the saints praise by knowing whom they exist for.

11.text: They will tell of the glory of Your kingdom, and speak of Your power,
11.amp: They shall speak [amar] of the glory [kabod] of Your kingdom [malkut], and talk [dabar] of Your power [geburah];
11.notes: The saints' conversation topic: kebod malkutekha (H3519, H4438), the kingdom's glory — the phrase the Lord's Prayer gathers up ('for Thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory'). What a people talks about is what it treasures; the chasidim talk realm and reign.

12.text: to make known to the sons of man His mighty acts, and the glorious majesty of His kingdom.
12.amp: To make known [yada] to the sons [ben] of men [adam] His mighty acts [geburah], and the glorious [kabod] majesty [hadar] of His kingdom [malkut].
12.notes: The kingdom-talk has a mission clause: le-hodia (H3045), to make known — not insider language but broadcast, aimed at the bene adam, the whole human family. Psalm 96's missionary charge in kingdom vocabulary.

13.text: Your kingdom is a kingdom of all the ages, and Your dominion endures through generation after generation.
13.amp: Your kingdom [malkut] is an everlasting kingdom ['a kingdom of all ages', malkut kol olamim, the KJV margin], and Your dominion [memshalah] endures throughout all generations [dor va-dor].
13.notes: malkut kol olamim (H4438, H5769): the kingdom of all the ages — the very words Daniel heard rehearsed to Nebuchadnezzar and wrote to the nations (cf. Daniel 4:3, 34), and the claim behind 'Thy kingdom come.' Empires are weather; this memshalah (H4475) is climate, dor va-dor.

14.text: The LORD upholds all who are falling, and raises up all who are bent down beneath their load.
14.amp: The LORD [YHWH] upholds [samak — supports, props] all that fall [naphal], and raises up [zaqaph — lifts erect] all those that be bowed down [kaphaph].
14.notes: The everlasting King's court business, verse one: the falling. samak (H5564), the leaning-support of Psalm 51:12, extended to KOL ha-nophelim — all of them — and zaqaph (H2210), the rare straightening-verb: the bent-double (kaphaph, H3721) stood upright again. Majesty measured by whom it stoops for (cf. Luke 13:11-13).

15.text: The eyes of all look and wait upon You, and You give them their food in its season.
15.amp: The eyes [ayin] of all wait ['look unto', sabar, the KJV margin — wait expectantly] upon You; and You give [natan] them their meat [okel — their food] in due season [et].
15.notes: The whole creation pictured at the table with its eyes on the Head: sabar (H7663), expectant waiting — sparrow, ox, and man alike. The okel (H400) arrives be-itto, in ITS season: provision on the Giver's calendar, which has never yet missed a feeding (cf. Psalm 104:27).

16.text: You open Your hand, and You satisfy the desire of every living thing.
16.amp: You open [pathach] Your hand [yad], and satisfy [saba] the desire [ratson] of every living thing [chay].
16.notes: The verse grace says over ten thousand dinner tables: one opened yad (H3027), and saba (H7646) — satisfaction, not scraps — reaching kol chay, every living thing. The universe is fed from an open palm, not a dispenser; providence is personal down to the nestlings.

17.text: The LORD is righteous in all His ways, and full of covenant kindness in all His works.
17.amp: The LORD [YHWH] is righteous [tsaddiq] in all His ways [derek], and holy ['merciful, bountiful', chasid, the KJV margin — covenant-kind] in all His works [maaseh].
17.notes: The double audit no creature passes and God passes twice: tsaddiq in KOL derek, chasid (H2623) in KOL maaseh — righteousness in every road He takes, covenant kindness in every act He performs. His ways and works never need the apology ours do.

18.text: The LORD is near to every one who calls upon Him — to all who call upon Him in truth.
18.amp: The LORD [YHWH] is nigh [qarov] unto all them that call [qara] upon Him, to all that call upon Him in truth [emeth].
18.notes: The nearness-promise at its widest: qarov (H7138) to ALL the callers — no rank, no résumé, one condition: be-emet (H571), in truth, the real self calling on the real God. Asaph's discovery (Psalm 73:28) issued as standing policy (cf. Deuteronomy 4:7; James 4:8).

19.text: He fulfills the desire of those who fear Him; He hears their cry, and He saves them.
19.amp: He will fulfil [asah] the desire [ratson] of them that fear [yare] Him: He also will hear [shama] their cry [shavah], and will save [yasha] them.
19.notes: The fear of the LORD reshapes desire until God can grant it whole: ratson (H7522) asah, desire done — Psalm 37:4's promise restated. And for the days desire collapses into a shavah, a cry: shama and yasha (H8085, H3467), heard and saved — the full range from longing to emergency, covered.

20.text: The LORD keeps watch over all who love Him, but all the wicked He will destroy.
20.amp: The LORD [YHWH] preserves [shamar — guards] all them that love [ahab] Him: but all the wicked [rasha] will He destroy [shamad].
20.notes: The acrostic's one dark letter, and even praise must include it: shamar (H8104) over the ohavim, the lovers — Psalm 121's watchman-verb — and shamad (H8045) for the rasha. The King who upholds all the falling is not neutral about those who make others fall; mercy's alphabet still ends its warnings honestly.

21.text: My mouth will speak out the praise of the LORD; let all flesh bless His holy name forever, world without end.
21.amp: My mouth [peh] shall speak [dabar] the praise [tehillah] of the LORD [YHWH]: and let all flesh [basar] bless [barak] His holy [qodesh] name [shem] for ever [olam] and ever [ad].
21.notes: David's last line in the Psalter's last Davidic psalm: his own peh committed first, then the summons swung wide — kol basar (H1320), all flesh, every mortal thing invited into the olam va-ed. The Tehillah ends by seeding the five Hallelujahs that close the book; Psalm 150's 'everything that has breath' is this verse fully grown.
